    "title": "Light-theme color of embedded-post username accidentally changed from 30% to 70% lightness",
    "body": "In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The PR converted it to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The first argument of `dark-light-choose` is the value used for light themes, so on light themes this text now renders at 70% lightness instead of the original 30% — the bold username in expanded 'in reply to' posts becomes far lighter and harder to read. Every analogous conversion in this PR preserves the original lightness in the first argument and uses the complementary value on `$secondary` for the dark branch (e.g. `.names span a` in common/base/topic-post.scss correctly became 30%/70%). The two lightness values here appear to have been swapped; it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`."

Because the first argument of `dark-light-choose` applies to light themes, the topic-map heading on mobile light themes is now rendered at 50% lightness instead of the intended 20%, making it much fainter. The desktop version of the same selector was converted correctly to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, so mobile is inconsistent. The light branch should remain at 20%: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`."

The first argument of `dark-light-choose` is the light-theme value, so on light themes the flag custom-message character counter now renders at 30% lightness instead of 70% — much darker than before. The desktop version of the same selector (desktop/modal.scss) was converted as 70%/30%, preserving the original light value, so mobile directly contradicts it. The analogous conversion in common/base/user.scss for `.user-small .name` kept the light value at 30% (30%/70%), so this deviates from the PR's stated goal of only changing the dark-theme branch.
